slides.texte_overlay:
everyday habits that build
bulletproof confidence

saying what you think

once a week, share an honest opinion you'd normally keep to yourself, calmly and kindly. people respect a clear view far more than nervous, polite agreement.

understanding people

learning a little psychology each day, like why we people please or how habits form, makes other people far less intimidating and much easier to read.
slides.texte_sophia:
understanding people

i spend 5 minutes a day on one idea from psychology, like why we people please. i do it with the Sophia app, and understanding people makes them so much less scary.

slides.texte_overlay:
asking them to explain

when a comment feels like a dig, ask calmly what they meant by it. most little jabs quickly fall apart the moment someone has to explain them out loud.

preparing your first line

before a hard conversation, write down the first sentence you want to say. walking in with a clear opening keeps your voice steady even when you're feeling nervous.

keeping no short

when you say no, give one reason or none at all. long explanations sound like you're asking for permission, while a short no sounds calm, kind and certain.
